properties.description:
The clients and their context. Context added or removed here is kept per client until you pass a different
context for that client – then your data wins

properties.name: client
properties.description: Id of the open client; empty opens the first

properties.name: me
properties.description: The signed-in person – author of new context

properties.name: tab
properties.description: The section shown: context, reports, financials or settings

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-client-change
events.description: A client was picked or created (`ClientContextClientChange`: `{ client }`); cancelable – prevented, `client` stays (controlled use)

events.name: tc-add-context
events.description: Context was added (`ClientContextAdd`: `{ client, text, files }`); cancelable – prevented, it isn't added here

events.name: tc-create-client
events.description: A client was created from the switcher (`ClientContextCreate`: `{ name }`); cancelable – prevented, it isn't created

events.name: tc-tab-change
events.description: The section changed (`ClientContextTabChange`: `{ tab }`); cancelable – prevented, `tab` stays

functions.name: defaultContextClients
functions.description: The sample clients shown when `clients` isn't set

functions.name: clientContextMatches
functions.description: Whether an entry matches the search (author, text, file names, report or app)

functions.name: clientContextMentionStart
functions.description: Where the "@" mention being typed starts, or null – an "@" at the start or after a space, up to the caret

props.name: clients
props.description:
The clients and their context. Context added or removed in the block is kept per client until you pass a
different context for that client – then your data wins

props.name: client
props.description: Id of the open client (controlled) – pass `onClientChange` with it. Leave undefined to start at `defaultClient` (the first)

props.name: defaultClient
props.description: The client open on mount when `client` isn't controlled – the first by default

props.name: onClientChange
props.description: A client was picked or created

props.name: tab
props.description: The section shown (controlled) – pass `onTabChange` with it

props.name: defaultTab
props.description: The section on mount when `tab` isn't controlled

props.name: onAddContext
props.type: (clientId: string, text: string, files: ContextFile[]) => void
props.description: Called when context is added, with the client, the text and any attached files

props.name: onCreateClient
props.description: Called when a client is created from the switcher

changelog: All 18 blocks are now elements – `tc-agent-gallery`, `tc-ai-side-pane`, `tc-ai-workspace`, `tc-app-directory`, `tc-client-context`, `tc-evidence-gallery`, `tc-header-nav`, `tc-invoice-credit`, `tc-kpi-board`, `tc-logo-marquee`, `tc-metrics-dashboard`, `tc-oversight-home`, `tc-pricing-plans`, `tc-publish-readiness`, `tc-red-team-finding`, `tc-task-board`, `tc-testimonial-wall`, `tc-uncertainty-mix` – so Angular (`trenchcoat/angular`), Vue, Svelte, plain HTML and generative UI get them like any component, with docs pages.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: inert
features.why: Closed and leaving parts are out of the tab order and hidden from screen readers.

features.name: :has()
features.why: Layout and state that depend on what's inside a part (an icon present, a focused field).

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: field-sizing
features.without: Text fields grow with their text. Without it they keep their minimum height and scroll.

features.name: scrollbar-width
features.without: Scrollbars keep the browser's default width.

features.name: @property
features.without: The registered custom properties don't interpolate, so the transitions and spins they drive jump to their end state.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.

features.name: overscroll-behavior: contain
features.without: Scrolling past the end of a list carries on scrolling the page.
